title: Scripture locked and sealed (Philoc. 2)
english: Scripture is [[locked and sealed >> Bible:Isaiah 29:11]]; the blesseds spoken in the singular and the plural must be weighed together, so that the reader does not treat the divine book as already open to every casual glance.
translator_notes: Copy-text Robinson 1893 Philocalia TEI (origen_tlg019.xml); no George Lewis 1911 wording.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Why twenty-two inspired books (Philoc. 3)
english: Origen counts the [[God-breathed >> Bible:2 Timothy 3:16]] books as twenty-two, matching the Hebrew letters, so that the church’s canon is taught as a closed, ordered library rather than an open heap.
translator_notes: Copy-text Robinson 1893 Philocalia TEI (origen_tlg019.xml); no George Lewis 1911 wording.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Solecisms and plain diction (Philoc. 4)
english: From the John commentary: the Evangelist’s rough solecisms are not a reason to despise the Gospel; the Word uses humble speech so that the [[treasure in earthen vessels >> Bible:2 Corinthians 4:7]] may be God’s power, not human polish.
translator_notes: Copy-text Robinson 1893 Philocalia TEI (origen_tlg019.xml); no George Lewis 1911 wording.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: One book, not many chatterings (Philoc. 5)
english: What looks like many books is one Scripture; verbosity is not the Spirit’s aim. The Word gathers the writings into one, as Christ gathers the scattered children of God.
translator_notes: Copy-text Robinson 1893 Philocalia TEI (origen_tlg019.xml); no George Lewis 1911 wording.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: One fitted instrument (Philoc. 6)
english: All divine Scripture is one perfect and fitted instrument of God; the many strings sound one harmony under the same Spirit.
translator_notes: Copy-text Robinson 1893 Philocalia TEI (origen_tlg019.xml); no George Lewis 1911 wording.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Persons speaking in Scripture (Philoc. 7)
english: Scripture’s speakers must be kept distinct — the Father, the Son, the Spirit, prophet, apostle — lest we confuse who says what and invent a voice the text never gave.
translator_notes: Copy-text Robinson 1893 Philocalia TEI (origen_tlg019.xml); no George Lewis 1911 wording.
